title: Biopsy of Secondary Angiosarcoma Arising in Native Mastectomy Skin of a Reconstructed Breast Without Prior Radiotherapy.
abstract: Secondary breast angiosarcoma usually develops after radiotherapy or in the setting of chronic lymphedema. We report a rare case of non-radiation-associated secondary cutaneous angiosarcoma arising in the native mastectomy skin overlying a reconstructed breast after immediate tissue expander placement and delayed deep inferior epigastric perforator flap reconstruction for breast cancer. The patient's clinical course, imaging, histopathological findings, and treatment were retrospectively reviewed. The clinicopathological features were compared with previously reported cases of angiosarcoma arising after breast reconstruction without radiotherapy before angiosarcoma onset. A 45-year-old woman underwent right mastectomy, axillary dissection, and immediate tissue expander placement for right breast cancer (T2N1M0, stage IIB), followed by delayed deep inferior epigastric perforator flap reconstruction 1 year later. No adjuvant radiotherapy was administered. Three years after the initial breast cancer surgery, progressive purpura and dark violaceous nodules developed in the native mastectomy skin. Skin biopsy confirmed cutaneous angiosarcoma. Histology showed atypical endothelial proliferation forming irregular vascular channels; tumor cells were positive for ETS-related gene and cluster of differentiation 34; the molecular immunology borstel-1 index was approximately 40%; and MYC proto-oncogene expression was observed in 60%-70% of tumor cells. Positron emission tomography-computed tomography showed no distant metastasis. Because the cutaneous disease was diffuse and surgical local control was judged difficult, multimodal treatment with pazopanib and radiotherapy (70 Gy) was initiated, followed by trastuzumab plus paclitaxel for local progression. No distant metastasis was present at the latest follow-up, although local control remained challenging. Persistent or progressive dermatitis-like lesions in postmastectomy breast skin should prompt early biopsy even in patients without prior radiotherapy.

title: Impact of body composition on clinical outcomes in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Abnormalities in body composition are common in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, their impact across different treatment modalities remains poorly understood. We systematically reviewed the prognostic value of body composition in patients with HCC, stratified by curative, locoregional, and systemic therapies. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (January 2015-March 2025) for studies reporting associations between CT/MRI or bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-assessed body composition and outcomes in HCC. Results Ninety-two studies were included (35 curative, 10 locoregional, 39 systemic, 8 mixed). Sarcopenia prevalence ranged from 6.4% to 62.8% (median study-level prevalence 38%-50% depending on treatment stratum). Sarcopenia independently predicted worse overall survival across all strata: curative (HR 1.52-3.76), locoregional (HR 1.72-2.51), and systemic therapies (HR 1.34-2.20). Sarcopenic obesity conferred the highest risk in the curative setting (HR up to 3.15). In systemic therapy, myosteatosis independently predicted mortality (HR 1.45-2.01), whereas visceral adiposity was protective (HR 0.56-0.66). In a random-effects meta-analysis of 44 studies, sarcopenia was associated with a pooled HR of 1.85 (95% CI 1.75-1.94; I2=0%), with consistent effects across curative (HR 1.86), locoregional (HR 2.10), and systemic strata (HR 1.71). Sarcopenia also predicted recurrence after curative treatment (pooled HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.61-1.82; k=14). Conclusions Sarcopenia predicts mortality in HCC, independently of treatment modality. Visceral adiposity appears detrimental after curative treatment but may be paradoxically protective during systemic therapy. Body composition should be integrated into clinical decision-making in HCC, though a clear consensus on measurement standardization is needed.

title: Presumed Primary CD79B+ Vitreoretinal Lymphoma Mimicking an Ischemia-Like Macular Lesion.
abstract: Purpose To report a case of presumed primary vitreoretinal lymphoma (PVRL) mimicking an ischemia-like macular lesion. Methods Single-patient case report. Results A 74-year-old male patient presented with sudden vision loss up to the hand-motion level in his right eye. Fundus examination revealed a creamy, white-colored, ischemic-appearing macular area excluding the foveal region. Numerous vitreous cells and snowball-like opacities were observed. No relative afferent pupillary defect was evident, and no intraorbital mass or signs of active inflammation were revealed by contrast-enhanced cranial magnetic resonance imaging. Fluorescence angiography revealed a late-phase leopard-spot pattern of hyperfluorescence, whereas optical coherence tomography showed banded subretinal exudates with hyperreflective, vitelliform lesions within the retinal pigment epithelium. Cytological examination of the vitreous was negative for malignant cells. Using next-generation sequencing, the multigene mutation analysis revealed pathogenic CD79B, BTG2, and PIM1 mutations, supporting the diagnosis of PVRL. Twenty-two months later, in response to visual acuity (best-corrected) reduction from 0.5 LogMAR (20/63) at baseline to hand motions, intravitreal methotrexate therapy was initiated in the left eye, which decreased the vitreous cell density. The right eye has since remained stable at 0.2 LogMAR (20/32). Conclusion Presumed PVRL can mimic ischemic-appearing macular lesions and should be considered in the differential diagnosis of atypical ischemic retinal lesions. A thorough diagnostic workup should include multimodal imaging and cranial magnetic resonance imaging. When cytology is inconclusive, molecular genetic testing via NGS becomes a crucial tool, particularly when clinical suspicion remains high.

title: Retinoschisis-Associated Retinal Detachment in Choroideremia: A Surgical Conundrum.
abstract: Purpose To describe a case of retinoschisis-associated retinal detachment (RD) in a patient with genetically confirmed choroideremia and discuss implications for surveillance and surgical management. Methods A case report of a 43-year-old man with genotypically confirmed choroideremia, CHM c.242_245 deletion, who developed rhegmatogenous RD following progression of peripheral retinoschisis. Multimodal imaging, including optical coherence tomography (OCT), B-scan ultrasonography, ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM), and fundus autofluorescence (AF) were utilized for diagnosis and surgical planning. Results The patient presented with acute visual decline from 20/20 Snellen to 20/100 Snellen in the affected eye following progression of temporal retinoschisis into the fovea. OCT demonstrated schisis cavities with subretinal fluid extending to the fovea. B-scan demonstrated shallow temporal subretinal fluid involving the macula, and UBM was suggestive of multiple small anterior holes within the retinoschisis, though these were not clearly identified on examination with indirect fundoscopy. Surgical repair with a high posterior encircling scleral buckle (#277 tire) with cryopexy achieved foveal reattachment, schisis cavity collapse, and visual recovery to 20/25 Snellen. Conclusions This case represents the first documented retinoschisis-associated RD in choroideremia. Progressive degeneration of the RPE, choroid, and retinal layers may create structural instability predisposing to RD when retinoschisis progresses. This mechanism should theoretically make surgical reattachment challenging. This case highlights the need for risk stratification, close follow-up, and early surgical intervention to prevent reversible vision loss in patients with retinoschisis, RD, and choroideremia.

title: Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy Prompting Diagnosis of Severe Aortic Regurgitation and Ascending Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Purpose To report a case of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) in which persistent paracentral dysfunction prompted cardiovascular investigation and diagnosis of severe aortic regurgitation, reduced ejection fraction, and ascending aortic aneurysm. Methods Longitudinal ophthalmic assessment, multimodal retinal imaging, Humphrey SITA Central 10-2 testing, cardiovascular evaluation, surgical findings, histopathology, and targeted aortopathy genetic testing were reviewed. Results A 44-year-old man presented with intermittent right-eye visual disturbance and persistent paracentral scotoma after non-explanatory neuroimaging. Unaided visual acuity remained 20/25 (6/7.5; approximately 0.10 logMAR) in each eye, intraocular pressure was 16-19 mmHg, and anterior-segment examination was unremarkable. Multimodal imaging supported PAMM, with structural OCT inner retinal/inner nuclear layer involvement and qualitative OCT-A/fluorescein angiographic parafoveal perfusion compromise. The affected inner retinal/inner nuclear layer region decreased from 45 micrometres to 32 micrometres. Right-eye Humphrey SITA Central 10-2 mean deviation worsened from -3.67 dB on 03 March 2020 to -5.19 dB in February 2026 despite unchanged central acuity. Cardiovascular assessment revealed a 5.5-cm ascending aortic aneurysm, severe aortic regurgitation, and left-ventricular ejection fraction of 49%. The patient underwent elective Bentall procedure, with postoperative ejection-fraction improvement to 55%. No postoperative quantitative OCT-A reperfusion claim is made. Conclusion PAMM may warrant systemic cardiovascular assessment when ocular findings do not fully explain persistent paracentral dysfunction. This case supports cautious multidisciplinary evaluation while avoiding unsupported claims of causality, quantitative OCT-A perfusion deficit, or postoperative retinal reperfusion.

title: Chorioretinal Scars in Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Following Prenatal Valacyclovir Therapy.
abstract: Background Congenital cytomegalovirus infection is the most common congenital infection. Ocular abnormalities affect approximately 14% of symptomatic children, but fewer than 1% of asymptomatic children. Prenatal valacyclovir reduces vertical transmission, but ophthalmic outcomes in exposed infants are poorly described. Methods We describe 2 neonates with congenital cytomegalovirus confirmed by amniotic fluid and urine polymerase chain reaction following first-trimester maternal primary infection. Both mothers received high-dose valacyclovir (8 g daily) from 13 weeks' gestation. Infants underwent neonatal evaluation, including dilated fundus examination and multimodal retinal imaging. Results Maternal treatment continued to 36 weeks in 1 pregnancy and was discontinued at 22 weeks in the other, after amniocentesis. Both infants had macular chorioretinal scarring. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated focal ellipsoid zone disruption in a clinically normal fellow eye in 1 infant. Cranial ultrasonography demonstrated caudothalamic and temporal lobe cysts with lenticulostriate vasculopathy in 1 infant and isolated lenticulostriate vasculopathy in the other. Physical and neurologic examinations, head circumference, full blood count, liver function and auditory brainstem responses were normal in both. Both were classified as symptomatic with central nervous system involvement on the basis of ocular findings and therefore received valganciclovir for a planned 6 months. Retinal findings were stable at 3 months. Conclusions Macular chorioretinal scarring was present in both infants despite otherwise limited clinical findings, and the extent of cranial imaging abnormality did not correspond to ocular involvement. Ophthalmologic examination determined disease classification and management. These observations do not permit conclusions regarding the effect of prenatal valacyclovir on ocular outcome.
